## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

HeartRateZoneCalculator — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/HeartRateZoneCalculator.kt

## Trigger

`determine` and `ranges` are already called — from `MainRacePageViewModel.onHeartRateReading` (app-wear/.../race/MainRacePageViewModel.kt:82) and from `ProfileViewModel.toUiState` (app-phone/.../ui/profile/ProfileViewModel.kt:194) — observed

## Today

`determine` and `ranges` both treat a `Profile` as valid once `hrMaxBpm` is
non-null: `val hrMaxBpm = profile.hrMaxBpm ?: return null` is the only guard.
`zoneThresholds` is mapped to boundaries in the order it is stored, with no
check that the values increase, and `plainZoneFor`/`ranges` index that list
assuming exactly four entries to match `HeartRateZone`'s five values —
nothing in `Profile.zoneThresholds : List<Int>`, in `ProfileEntity`, or in
the sync payload (`PayloadCodec`) constrains its size or order.

A zero `hrMaxBpm` passes the guard; every boundary becomes
`(threshold / 100.0 * 0).roundToInt() == 0`, and `plainZoneFor`'s reversed
loop returns `ZONE_5` for any reading `>= 0`, i.e. almost every reading.

A disordered `zoneThresholds` (e.g. descending) is mapped to boundaries in
the same disorder; `plainZoneFor`'s reversed scan then returns whichever
zone's boundary the reading happens to clear first, which can be a low zone
for a high reading.

A `zoneThresholds` list not of length four is exercised elsewhere in the
codebase already — `PayloadCodecCrossModuleTest.kt:23` (both app-wear and
app-phone) builds a `Profile` with `zoneThresholds = emptyList()`. Against
such a profile, `ranges`' `thresholds[index - 1]` throws
`IndexOutOfBoundsException` past the first entry, and `determine`'s
`boundaries[previousZone.ordinal]` / `boundaries[plainZone.ordinal]` throw
under the same condition whenever `previousZone` or `plainZone` is a higher
zone than the boundary list can index.

Only the null-`hrMaxBpm` case is treated as "this profile cannot yield
zones" and answered with an explicit `null` (`determine`) or `null`
(`ranges`) — both already documented in the KDoc and both already handled
by their callers (`activeZone = HeartRateZoneCalculator.determine(...)` is
nullable in `MainRacePageViewModel`; `ranges?.let { toZoneRows(it) } ?:
emptyList()` in `ProfileViewModel`).

## Expected

`determine` and `ranges` treat a zero or negative `hrMaxBpm`, a
`zoneThresholds` that is not strictly increasing, and a `zoneThresholds`
whose size does not equal `HeartRateZone.values().size - 1` the same way
they already treat a null `hrMaxBpm`: as a profile that cannot yield zones,
answered with the same explicit `null` result on both functions, never by
throwing and never by returning a zone computed from the invalid values.
The KDoc on `determine` and on `ranges` states this — that any of these four
conditions determines no active zone / no ranges — so the contract covers
every case that can reach the function, not only the one it names today.
